proofs.full_local_argument: For t>0, every derivative of exp(-1/t) is exp(-1/t) times a polynomial in 1/t and tends to 0 as t decreases to 0; hence eta extends smoothly by zero. eta(t)+eta(1-t)>0 for every real t. Therefore chi is smooth, takes values in [0,1], equals zero for t<=0 and one for t>=1; rho has the stated smooth even plateau. Its positive-order derivatives vanish off a compact transition region and are bounded, so Bp is finite. Evenness gives oddness of h_tau. Differentiation gives h_tau'=rho(s/tau) and h_tau^(k)=tau^(1-k)rho^(k-1)(s/tau). Thus 0<=h_tau'<=1 and |h_tau(s)|<=|s|. For s>=0, s-h_tau(s)=tau integral_0^(s/tau)(1-rho(u))du is between 0 and tau because the integrand is in [0,1] and vanishes for u>=1. Oddness proves the absolute bound for negative s and consequently h_tau(s)>=s-tau for every s. The integral vanishes on the flat interval; smoothness makes every derivative zero at its endpoints as well. For s>=tau the integral deficit is b_tau; since rho=0 on [0,1/2], b_tau is between tau/2 and tau. The displayed derivative formula gives ||h_tau^(p)||infinity<=Bp tau^(1-p); the fundamental theorem of calculus gives the asserted Lipschitz bound. Orthogonality and 1-Lipschitzness imply ||T_V(x)-T_V(y)||^2=q^2 sum_{i=1}^{m-1}|h_tau(<vi,x>)-h_tau(<vi,y>)|^2<=q^2||x-y||^2. Also ||T_V(x)||^2<=c^2+q^2||x||^2<=R^2 for ||x||<=R, since c^2/R^2=1/(4m) and 1-q^2=1/m-1/(4m^2)>=1/(4m). Cauchy–Schwarz then gives <F_V(x)-F_V(y),x-y>>=lambda(1-q)||x-y||^2. For unit u1,...,up, D^pT_V(x)[u1,...,up]=q sum_i h_tau^(p)(<vi,x>)(product_j<vi,uj>)v_{i+1}. Its squared norm is at most q^2 Bp^2 tau^(2-2p) sum_i product_j|<vi,uj>|^2<=q^2 Bp^2 tau^(2-2p): bound all factors but j=1 by one and sum the remaining squared coordinates using orthonormality. Since p>=2, D^p of the identity vanishes. Therefore ||D^p F_V||op<=lambda q Bp tau^(1-p)<=Lp; integration on any segment proves the D^(p-1) Lipschitz estimate. Banach contraction gives the unique fixed point of T_V, hence unique zero of F_V, and ball invariance places it in X. T_V takes values in span(V), so the zero has no outside-frame component. Its coordinates satisfy s1=c,s_{i+1}=q h_tau(si). Positivity and |h_tau(s)|<=|s| yield 0<=si<=c q^(i-1) and ||xstar||^2<=c^2/(1-q^2)=R^2/[4(1-1/(4m))]<=R^2/3. Iterating h_tau(s)>=s-tau gives si>=c q^(i-1)-q tau sum_{j=0}^{i-2}q^j. Bernoulli gives q^(i-1)>=1-(i-1)/(2m)>=1/2, and the subtracted sum is at most m tau=c/8. Thus si>=3c/8, also trivially for i=1; summing squares gives ||xstar||>=3R/16. In the interior N_X(x)={0}. On the boundary N_X(x)={ax:a>=0}, and <F_V(x),x>=lambda(R^2-<T_V(x),x>)>=0 by ball invariance and Cauchy–Schwarz. Hence ||F_V(x)+ax||^2=||F_V(x)||^2+2a<F_V(x),x>+a^2R^2>=||F_V(x)||^2, with equality at a=0. This proves the all-ball residual identity. Finally write si=<vi,x>, e=x-T_V(x), e1=s1-c and ei=si-q h_tau(s_{i-1})<=si-q s_{i-1}+q tau for i>=2. Let wi=q^(m-i) and w=sum_i wi vi. Multiplying these inequalities and telescoping yields <w,e><=sm-c q^(m-1)+q tau sum_{i=2}^m q^(m-i)<=tau/2-c/2+m tau=tau/2-3c/8<=-c/4, since q^(m-1)>=1/2, m tau=c/8 and tau/2<=c/16. Since ||w||<=sqrt(m), Cauchy–Schwarz gives ||e||>=|<w,e>|/||w||>=c/(4sqrt(m))=R/(8m). This argument only uses frame coordinates of e, so an outside-frame component of x does not invalidate it. Multiply by lambda and use the residual identity and tau=R/(16m^(3/2)) to obtain the exact stated obstruction.

assumptions: p>=2 and N>=1 integers; Lp,R>0; integer d>=m=N+1; V orthonormal.
The norm is Euclidean and tensors use induced multilinear operator norm.
Hidden-slab conclusion additionally requires x in X and |<vm,x>|<=tau/2; no restriction on outside-frame components.
statement.conclusion: rho is even C-infinity in [0,1], zero on |u|<=1/2 and one on |u|>=1. h_tau is odd C-infinity, 0<=h_tau'<=1, |h_tau(s)|<=|s|, |s-h_tau(s)|<=tau and h_tau(s)>=s-tau. h_tau and ALL derivatives vanish on [-tau/2,tau/2], endpoints included. h_tau^(k)(s)=tau^(1-k)rho^(k-1)(s/tau),k>=1; Lip(h_tau^(p-1))<=Bp tau^(1-p). For s>=tau,h_tau(s)=s-b_tau, b_tau=tau integral_0^1(1-rho(u))du in [tau/2,tau]. T_V is globally q-contractive and maps X into itself. F_V is globally lambda(1-q)=lambda/(2m)-strongly monotone, C-infinity, and Lip(D^(p-1)F_V)<=Lp without a dimension factor. Unique zero xstar=sum_i si vi has s1=c,s_{i+1}=q h_tau(si), and 3R/16<=||xstar||<=R/sqrt(3). For EVERY x in X, boundary included, r_tan(x)=||F_V(x)||. On the hidden slab, r_tan(x)>=lambda R/(8m)=Lp R^p/[8Bp16^(p-1)m^((3p-1)/2)]. Strong monotonicity tends to zero with N at fixed p,Lp,R; it is not a uniform class assumption.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Euclidean R^d; ||A||op=sup_{||u_j||<=1}||A[u1,...,uk]|| for multilinear tensors. X=B_2^d(R), x0=0. N_X(x)={n:<n,z-x><=0 for all z in X}; r_tan(x)=dist(0,F_V(x)+N_X(x)). eta(t)=exp(-1/t) for t>0, otherwise 0; chi(t)=eta(t)/(eta(t)+eta(1-t)); rho(u)=chi((4u^2-1)/3). Bp=max{1,||rho^(p-1)||infinity}, h_tau(s)=tau integral_0^(s/tau)rho(u)du. m=N+1,q=1-1/(2m),c=R/(2sqrt(m)),tau=c/(8m),lambda=Lp tau^(p-1)/Bp. For any orthonormal V=(v1,...,vm), T_V(x)=cv1+q sum_{i=1}^{m-1}h_tau(<vi,x>)v_{i+1}, F_V(x)=lambda(x-T_V(x)).
statement.parameter_domains: tau=R/(16m^(3/2))>0,0<q<1,lambda>0; p fixed for p-dependent constants.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every admissible parameter choice and every orthonormal frame, all stated properties hold. No randomness required; constants do not depend on dimension or frame.
